name: Running page header/footer (start:body markers)
description: A page header and footer that repeat on EVERY printed page, declared as block trees under page.header / page.footer. Emitted via the official BIP body markers: header blocks before <?start:body?>, footer blocks after <?end body?>.
whenToUse: Any print report needing page furniture - report/company name on top, confidentiality or legal line at the bottom - independent of where the body paginates. Fields (with format masks) work inside the bands.
intents: repeat the company name at the top of every page
put a confidential notice in the page footer
running header with the report title and run date on all pages
footer on every page of the pdf

requires.dataShape: any; header/footer fields resolve from the ROOT context (root-level elements like REPORT_TITLE, RUN_DATE)

composition.notes: page.header/page.footer sit BESIDE blocks on the rtf layout spec (inside the page object), not inside blocks[]. Combine with any body. For 'Page x of y' numbers in the footer see lp:technique:rtf-raw-page-x-of-y.

pitfalls: Do NOT hand-build raw \sectd or {\header...} RTF groups - they make BIP tags STOP MERGING (literal/empty output). page.header/page.footer is the supported mechanism.
page.header/page.footer take BLOCK trees (same shapes as blocks[]), not strings.
Everything in page.header repeats on every page - one-time cover content belongs in blocks[], not the header.

name: Format masks: date/number/currency on field AND expr columns
description: Engine-validated format masks - <?format-date/number/currency:VALUE;'MASK'?> - applied via format:{type,mask} on table columns (plain field columns AND computed expr columns) and on {field,format} runs in paragraphs/headings.
whenToUse: Whenever raw data values (ISO dates, unformatted numbers) must print as business values. Apply the mask at EVERY point a value is shown - expr columns need it exactly like field columns.
intents: format the dates as 15-Jan-2026 in the table
show amounts with thousands separators and two decimals
currency format on the amount due column
the computed column prints raw numbers - format it too

requires.dataShape: dates as ISO yyyy-MM-dd (xsd:date) in the output XML; numbers delivered unformatted by SQL

composition.notes: omitting mask falls back to engine defaults: XDODEFDATE / #,##0.00 / XDODEFCC

pitfalls: An expr column is STILL a value to mask - {expr:'QTY * UNIT_PRICE'} without format ships raw numbers (verified past failure: raw ISO timestamps in rendered tables).

Two mask families are accepted - Oracle-style 'DD-MON-YYYY' and Java-style 'dd-MMM-yyyy' - pick ONE per mask, never blend them. Render-observed: 'DD-MON-YYYY' prints 06-Aug-2026 (the engine title-cases the month, it does NOT print AUG).
Masks format at display time only - the SQL still delivers clean typed values; do not TO_CHAR in SQL and mask again.

sourceRefs.verifiedIn: shard harness render PASS + PNG check 2026-08-06: both mask families + masked expr column verified visually

name: Sort within a repeating region (table forEach / forEach block)
description: Engine-validated <?sort:EXPR;'order';data-type='number'?> tags emitted right after the for-each opens, via sort:[{expr,order,dataType}] on a table (with forEach) or on a forEach block.
whenToUse: Order rows in the layout when the SQL order cannot serve - typically one dataset feeding SEVERAL differently-ordered sections. When only one order is needed, prefer ORDER BY in SQL.
intents: sort the lines by amount descending
order the table by vendor name
largest amounts first in the report
alphabetical vendor list from the same data

composition.notes: sort is a property OF the repeating spec (table.sort / forEach.sort) - there is no standalone sort block; multiple keys = multiple array entries in priority order

pitfalls: The separator before data-type is a SEMICOLON - <?sort:AMOUNT;'descending';data-type='number'?>; a comma is rejected by the engine ('Incorrect XPath').
Numeric sorts NEED dataType:'number' - a text sort puts 980.00 above 15,000.00.
Sort keys are evaluated in the group's row context - use line-level element names.

sourceRefs.verifiedIn: shard harness render PASS + PNG check 2026-08-06: descending numeric table + alphabetical forEach list from deliberately shuffled fixture

name: Conditional content: if / choose / context conditionals (if@CTX)
description: if{test,blocks} emits <?if:test?>...<?end if?>; choose{whens[{test,blocks}],otherwise} emits <?choose:?>/<?when?>/<?otherwise?>; adding context:'inlines'|'row'|'cell'|'column'|'section' emits <?if@CTX:test?> to scope exactly what gets hidden (the close stays plain <?end if?>).
whenToUse: Show/hide presentation by data: warning paragraphs for overdue rows, value-band texts, inline badges, whole-section gates. For hiding a TABLE COLUMN use the per-column guard instead (lp:technique:rtf-column-guard).
intents: show a warning only when the document is overdue
different text depending on the amount band
display ON HOLD next to held documents only
hide this section when the flag is N

composition.notes: if/choose blocks nest freely inside forEach; tests are XPath in the enclosing context

runs: ACTION REQUIRED: this document is overdue.

pitfalls: Tests are relative to the ENCLOSING for-each context - STATUS='OVERDUE' inside forEach G_ROW reads the current row's element.
The close of a context conditional is plain <?end if?> - never <?end if@row?>.
A conditional with an SQL equivalent (CASE WHEN) belongs in SQL - keep template conditionals for presentation, not computation (simplicity contract).

name: RTF dashboard grid: two charts side-by-side
description: A grid block (borderless RTF table; column widths in TWIPS) with one row of two cells, each hosting a chart block - the print answer to a 2-up dashboard band.
whenToUse: Print/PDF dashboards wanting two charts on one band (pie + bar, trend + breakdown). If the ask is chart BESIDE A REPEATING DETAIL TABLE, that layout is XPT-only - an RTF grid cell cannot host a repeating table.
intents: pie chart and bar chart side by side on the pdf
two charts in one row of the print dashboard
chart left chart right layout in rtf

requires.dataShape: one detail-grain group; each chart aggregates it per its own group.by

conflicts: repeating detail table inside an RTF grid cell (that shape is xpt-only: lp:technique:xpt-grid-chart-table)
composition.notes: cells can also hold heading/paragraph/image; a table in a cell renders as a COMPACT non-repeating panel only

pitfalls: RTF grid columns are TWIPS (1440/inch; default printable width 9360) - pixel values like 560/1044 produce micro-cells. The PIXEL grid is the XPT one.
Size each chart to FIT its cell: chart widthPx*15 twips must be <= its column width (300px = 4500 twips fits a 4680 column).
A chart's group.select stays ABSOLUTE (/DATA_DS/G_ROW) - a grid cell does not open a for-each context.
A select matching 0 nodes renders a normal-looking frame with the literal 'No data to display' - LOOK at the chart areas after render.

name: RTF dashboard grid: chart | KPI text panel
description: A grid row pairing a chart cell with a shaded KPI panel: headings + big bold paragraphs bound to a single-row SQL totals group. The print replacement for the XPT kpis row.
whenToUse: Print dashboard band with one chart plus 2-4 headline numbers. KPI values come from a single-row totals group computed in SQL - never template math.
intents: chart with the key totals next to it
headline numbers beside the graph on the pdf
kpi cards and a chart in one row for print

requires.dataShape: detail group for the chart + a SINGLE-ROW totals group (e.g. G_TOTALS with SQL SUM/COUNT columns) for the KPI panel
requires.preAggregation: KPI values as SQL aggregate columns (SUM OVER / COUNT), not sum() template expressions

conflicts: headline KPIs rendered as a table (banned - they are big bold paragraphs in a shaded cell)
composition.notes: swap cells or add rows for more bands; combine with lp:technique:rtf-landscape for wide dashboards

pitfalls: Bind KPI paragraphs by ABSOLUTE path ({field:'/DATA_DS/G_TOTALS/TOTAL_AMOUNT'}) - there is no enclosing forEach inside a grid cell.
Headline KPIs are NOT a table - big bold paragraphs (style.size) in a shaded cell (bg) read as cards.
Grid columns in twips; cell bg takes #hex.

name: Header fields band (label: value pairs above the lines table)
description: The invoice-style band of bold 'Label: value' lines above the line-item table - paragraphs pairing a bold literal run ({text,bold:true}) with a field run. The rtf layout spec's headerFields key generates exactly this band.
whenToUse: Document-shaped output (PO, invoice, remittance) where a handful of master fields sit above the lines. For one document per master node, wrap band + table in a forEach (see lp:technique:rtf-invoice-shape).
intents: supplier and po number above the lines table
invoice header details on top then the items
label value pairs at the top of the document

requires.dataShape: master fields at the ROOT (single document) or on the outer group node (one document per node)

composition.notes: convenience path: zRtfLayout headerFields:[{label,field|expr}] + linesGroup/columns emits this same shape (empty label = value only, no colon); use explicit blocks when the band needs anything beyond plain pairs

pitfalls: Bold the LABEL run only ({text:'Supplier: ',bold:true}) - a paragraph-level style bolds the value too.
Empty label means value-only - never emit an orphan ': ' prefix.
Inside an outer forEach the band fields go RELATIVE to the group node (no leading /).

name: Static embedded PNG image (logo/banner)
description: An image block embeds literal PNG bytes (base64) into the RTF as \pict\pngblip with optional widthTwips/heightTwips scaling and alignment. Static bytes only - the image travels inside the template.
whenToUse: Fixed chrome: company logo, banner, signature block. ASK the user to provide the real PNG bytes; use a neutral placeholder until they do.
intents: put our logo at the top of the report
company banner image on the letterhead
embed a static image in the template

composition.notes: an image block also works inside page.header (logo on every page) and inside a grid cell

runs: . Replace the placeholder PNG above with the customer's logo bytes.

pitfalls: Dynamic per-row images (url:{...} alt-text binding, atlas #28) are NOT supported by the generator - static bytes only; say so instead of faking it.
NEVER fabricate a real-looking logo - ship the neutral placeholder and ask the user for their PNG.
widthTwips/heightTwips scale the render (1440 twips = 1 inch); omitted, the PNG renders at intrinsic px @96dpi.
PNG only (\pngblip) - convert JPEG/GIF before embedding.

name: Landscape page geometry (widthTwips > heightTwips)
description: Landscape print by page geometry alone: page:{widthTwips:15840, heightTwips:12240} (11in x 8.5in) - the correct DSL surface. KNOWN GAP: the current builder emits \paperw/\paperh before the font table, where the BIP engine IGNORES them, so output today stays letter portrait until a one-line builder fix lands (geometry after the font/color tables is render-proven to work).
whenToUse: Wide tables (7+ columns), two-chart dashboard bands, anything that clips or wraps in portrait. Shrink marginTwips (720 = 0.5in) to buy more printable width. Until the builder fix ships, do NOT promise landscape output - say the geometry key exists but is currently ignored by the engine, and offer narrower columns or smaller fonts as the interim.
intents: make the report landscape
the table is too wide for portrait
rotate the page so all columns fit

composition.notes: combines with any body; plan table column widths against the new printable width (pageWidth - 2*margin)

pitfalls: BUILDER BUG (2026-08-06, render-proven): page geometry (\paperw/\paperh/\marg*) is emitted BEFORE {\fonttbl} and the engine ignores it there - PDF stays 612x792pt portrait and marginTwips is ignored too. Emitting the same control words AFTER the font/color tables renders true 792x612 landscape with fields intact. Raw-run workarounds do not work (doc-format words in the body and \sectd/\pgwsxn section geometry are all ignored).
Landscape is nothing but width > height - there is no 'orientation' key.
Re-plan column widths for the landscape printable width (15840 - 2*720 = 14400 twips) - portrait widths leave a third of the page blank.
Mixed portrait+landscape sections in ONE template are not supported by the generator (corpus does it with \sect breaks; atlas #59 partial).

name: Column guard: show/hide a whole table column by a flag
description: Per-column guard:{context:'column'|'cell', test} wraps that column's header AND body cells with <?if@column:test?>...<?end if?> opened and closed CONTIGUOUSLY inside each cell, so the column shows or hides as a unit.
whenToUse: Parameter- or data-driven column visibility: cost columns only for buyers, ratings only when a PSHOW flag is Y. Corpus-verbatim shape: <?if@column://PSHOWWORKERRATINGSFLAG='Y'?>.
intents: hide the cost column unless the flag is Y
only show ratings when the parameter allows it
optional column controlled by a report parameter

requires.dataShape: the flag as a root-level element (reference it as //FLAG or an absolute path so it resolves from inside the row context)

composition.notes: guard is a COLUMN property; the if-block form with context:'column' exists but the per-column guard is the right tool for tables (wraps header+body contiguously)

pitfalls: The guard lives ON the column definition - do not wrap the whole table in an if block with context:'column'; the conditional must open and close INSIDE each cell, never span the row.
Use //FLAG (or an absolute path) in the test - a bare FLAG resolves against the ROW group and silently never matches.
context 'cell' hides only the body cell content; 'column' is the whole-column corpus shape (header included).

name: Subtemplate import + callTemplate (unconditional import, optionally wrapped call)
description: imports:[...] emits <?import:xdoxsl:///<catalog path>.xsb?loc=en?> UNCONDITIONALLY at the very top of the body; a callTemplate block emits <?call-template:NAME?> where the shared content should appear - optionally condition-wrapped via when.
whenToUse: Shared chrome (footers, terms blocks, notification headers) maintained once in a catalog .xsb and reused across templates. Build the .xsb itself with createSubtemplateFile (templates:[{name,blocks}]).
intents: reuse the shared footer subtemplate in this report
import the common blocks and call the note template
conditionally call a catalog subtemplate

composition.notes: the .xsb defines <?template:NAME?>...<?end template?> entries; ONE import serves any number of callTemplate blocks

pitfalls: Imports must NEVER sit inside if/choose - an import resolves at compile time; a conditional or unresolvable import kills the WHOLE template. Condition the CALL, not the import.
A call-template name that no import defines is an XSL compile error (template not found) - the whole render fails, not a silent no-op.
Parameterized calls (param@begin / with-param, atlas #21) are NOT supported by the generator yet - calls are parameterless.
The when test evaluates at the call site's context (root after top-level blocks).

name: Page x of y footer (raw Word PAGE/NUMPAGES fields)
description: 'Page 1 of 7' numbering via raw-idiom LEAF runs: the Word field codes for PAGE and NUMPAGES embedded as {raw} runs inside the page.footer paragraph. BIP maps them to per-page numbers at render. No first-class DSL key yet - hence partial.
whenToUse: Any multi-page print document that needs page numbering. Keep the raw runs leaf-level (the two field codes only) - never build loops or conditionals in raw.
intents: page 1 of 7 at the bottom of each page
number the pages in the footer
show total page count on every page

composition.notes: composes with any page.footer content; the surrounding literals ('Page ', ' of ') are normal string runs

pitfalls: raw runs are emitted UNESCAPED - keep them to these two field codes; structural RTF in raw (loops, sectd, header groups) is banned.
The literal 1 inside {\fldrslt 1} is only Word's cached preview - BIP replaces it per page at render.
Per-section page-number RESTART (initial-page-number, atlas #7) is a separate unsupported capability - this idiom numbers the whole document.

name: Invoice shape: master forEach + header band + lines table + totals (page per document)
description: The classic two-level document: outer forEach over the master/invoice group (splitByPage = one document per page), header-band paragraphs, then the lines table whose shaded totals row sums the CURRENT master's lines via the relative sum(G_LINE/AMOUNT) evaluated in the parent context.
whenToUse: Invoices, POs, remittances, delivery notes - one document per master node with its own lines and totals. Hierarchies deeper than master>lines escalate to lp:archetype:statement-run / lp:technique:rtf-multilevel-blocks.
intents: classic invoice layout with lines and a total
one invoice per page with its line items
po print with header block lines and total per document

requires.dataShape: nested output groups G_INVOICE > G_LINE via datamodel groupBy; master fields on the invoice node
requires.preAggregation: grand totals ACROSS invoices belong in SQL (ROLLUP/SUM OVER), not the template

composition.notes: the rtf layout spec's convenience keys (title/headerFields/outerGroup/linesGroup/columns/totals/sort/splitByPage) generate exactly this block tree - prefer them for the plain invoice; drop to blocks[] to add anything beyond the shape

pitfalls: The lines path is RELATIVE (G_LINE) - the builder REJECTS an absolute inner group under an outer forEach: every outer iteration would repeat ALL lines and totals would aggregate globally.
The totals row sits OUTSIDE the for-each (parent context) - sum(G_LINE/AMOUNT) totals the current invoice only; a leading / makes it a document-wide total.

A totals cell has no format key - to mask the aggregate, make the expr the format tag itself: expr:"format-number:sum(G_LINE/AMOUNT);'#,##0.00'" (render-verified); a bare sum() prints 1730.5 unformatted.
splitByPage on the OUTER forEach = one page per document; on the table block it means one page per LINE - a different technique (lp:technique:rtf-splitbypage-table).
Bind placeholders (G_INVOICE, INVOICE_NUM) to YOUR datamodel's output tree before building.

sourceRefs.verifiedIn: shard harness render PASS + PNG check 2026-08-06: two pages, one invoice each, per-invoice totals 1,730.50 and 4,750.00

name: One page per repeated ROW (forEach split around a static 1-row table)
description: One printed page per data ROW: a forEach over the row group with splitByPage:true wrapping a STATIC 1-row table - every iteration re-emits the column header plus that row's values, then breaks. This is the render-verified page-per-row shape; the table-level splitByPage key exists but paginates degenerately (see pitfalls).
whenToUse: Ticket/voucher/label-per-page output where each ROW is the whole printed unit: delivery tickets, gate passes, one-line confirmations. Every page gets the header row + one record.
intents: one page per ticket row
print each record on its own page
page break after every table row

requires.dataShape: a flat repeating group where ONE row = one printed unit

conflicts: forEach splitByPage over a MASTER group (that is page-per-GROUP-with-children - the invoice/statement shape)
composition.notes: the inner table is STATIC (no forEach key) - the wrapping forEach provides the repetition; cell fields resolve in the current row context

pitfalls: ENGINE QUIRK (render-verified 2026-08-06): splitByPage directly ON a table's row loop does NOT deliver one page per row - the break lands so the header row ends page 1 ALONE and the last two rows share the final page ([header][row1]...[rowN-1 rowN]). Use this forEach + static-1-row-table shape instead - true page-per-row with the header repeated.
The inner table must be STATIC (no forEach) - adding forEach would nest a second loop inside the row iteration.
The break tag must stay CONTIGUOUS immediately before <?end for-each?> (the builder places it) - hand-moving it breaks all but the first iteration.
